chunks: Abu al-Bakhtari narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, that ʿAlī عليه السلام said:
In emancipation, the blind, the one-eyed, and the crippled are not permissible; while the one with a paralyzed limb and the lame are permissible.

key_terms.الْأَشَلُّ: the person with a paralyzed limb
key_terms.الْعَتَاقِ: emancipation or manumission of a slave

ai.seo_question: Which physical conditions affect the validity of emancipation in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding which slaves are valid for emancipation in the context of ʿitq. It distinguishes between certain severe physical defects that invalidate this form and others that do not.
